findings.consequence: The first-global descriptor and shared cleanup deadline can start later than the retained successful waitpid observation, violating protocol terminal_lifecycle.failure_observation_time and earliest_failure+10. Exact extracted supervisor/notify/pool proofs retain a worker report at 99.75 but produce first_failure=100.0/until=110.0, instead of 99.75/109.75. Both rc=1 and raw status 9/rc=-9 discriminate. No accepted receipt, actual OS overrun, survivor, performance, or training failure is claimed.
findings.fix_direction: Preserve the validated abnormal worker direct-wait source timestamp through the inner failure path before later IPC/probe/file operations; keep earlier guard/latch/peer sources, existing cap, ACK/write rules, mandatory-first ordering and single worker_wait send semantics.
findings.mechanism: supervise_owned takes child.report, sends worker_wait, checks absence and reads long-worker-result.json before checking the abnormal raw outcome. No source-stamped error is made from report.observed_monotonic. A missing result (normal for abrupt death) or another intervening error enters observed_failure with no descriptor, so it selects the later catch time. Execution.pump validates and retains the worker_wait but does not fail the pool for its abnormal returncode, so the outer does not recover the earlier source time.
findings.proof_limits: Small exact AST extractions with fake child, clock, channel and absence inputs. The signaled-worker case uses the real extracted read_json on an actually missing owned fixture file. No real signal, waitpid, process-group or ML execution.
findings.title: Retain the abnormal worker wait observation before later IPC and file IO
findings.trigger: Worker exits with raw returncode outside (0,2), without an earlier worker failure packet, guard, latch, or peer descriptor. Its live supervisor obtains a direct wait report before later worker_wait IPC, group probing, or result-file reading.
